main_text.head: INSTITUTIONUM METAPHYSICARUM,
Tractatus Secundus,
QUI EST DE Subjecto, seu Trunco.
CAPUT. I. DE Constitutione & Essentia.
main_text.p: 1. SEcundum ordinem Principiorum & Affectionum, ad calcem superioris tractatus propositum, primum agmen ducit, Constitutio, cum suis affectionibus ex ipsa de Ente demonstrandis. Primò igitur dicendum de Constitutionis, tum nomine, tum re.

2. Nomen à constituendo, & quasi simul ordinando habet, primitus desumtum ab eis, quae ex unione sensibilium partium esse suum obtinebant, unde non secus ac plurimi alii termini ad Metaphysicam traductum,

page.notes: The initial S is a large woodcut initial, transcribed as "SE" joined to the word "Ecundum" as "SEcundum". Pages are printed in roman with italic passages. The last line of the page is right-aligned and ends the word "traductum" with a hyphen split ("tradu-" / "ctum"), read here as "traductum" from the continuation "ctum," shown in the scan as "stum"; the final word is partly illegible in the scan and should be checked against the original.
